newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan aims to revive its stagnant gold sector.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan aims to revive its stagnant gold sector.

text.p: Kazakhstan plans to increase its gold output sharply from 1998, despite an expected slight fall this year, a government official said on Wednesday.

"We are working on a new programme for developing Kazakhstan's gold industry to 2005 and we have a very optimistic picture," Boris Sadchikov, deputy head of the industry branches development department, told Reuters.
He said Kazakhstan planned to boost annual gold production to 20 tonnes within the next five years and to 40 tonnes by 2005.
Output of the yellow metal was likely to grow next year to 13-14 tonnes, although this year the former Soviet republic would produce around 10 tonnes, slightly below last year's 10.3 tonnes.

The government has signed over 30 contracts with private companies, including foreign ones, for development and exploitation of gold deposits. Sadchikov said it would take investors at least a year to complete technical studies.

"Many deposits and mines now have new proprietors... including foreign companies with their own approaches...Under the circumstances, the fall (in output this year) is only natural and there is nothing terrible about it," he said.
Under a previous programme from 1992, Kazakhstan planned to raise gold output to 40 tonnes in 1997 and to over 50 tonnes by the year 2000.
The general economic crisis and lack of investment hampered this goal, but officials still say the sector holds great promise.
"In line with our preliminary estimates, we expect up to $1.5 billion in investment in the gold industry by 2005...Annual investment is likely to be $150-170 million," Sadchikov said.
He said Kazakhstan's largest Vasilkonskoye gold deposit, with proven reserves of at least 400 tonnes, offered investment opportunities.
"Vasilkovskoye currently produces around 600 kg (1,330 lbs) of gold a year, and this is too little," he said.
Kazakhstan -- a vast steppeland Central Asian state with a population of just 16.7 million people -- has the world's seventh largest proven gold reserves, around 1,000 tonnes.
But there may be much more.
"According to our estimated gold reserves of 10,000 tonnes, Kazakhstan ranks second in the world following South Africa," Sadchikov said, quoting a government estimate.

He stressed that in contrast to Soviet times, when Kazakhstan was just a cheap supplier of concentrated auriferous ores for refineries in other parts of the Soviet Union, the country now refined over 90 percent of its output. --Almaty Newsroom, +7 3272 509410
